_comment: datafusion-tracing is published on crates.io, so hosted rustdoc JSON exists -- and is not
enough. lib.rs declares `mod options;` and `mod rule_options;` PRIVATE and selectively
re-exports only InstrumentationOptions and RuleInstrumentationOptions. Both builders are
therefore public types in private modules: docs.rs serves 404 for them, they are absent
from all.html, and the rustdoc JSON carries the structs with zero impl blocks. Seventeen
public methods -- six of which the crate's own README quick-start chains -- exist in no
So each subject crate is captured TWICE: once from docs.rs (the published surface) and once
locally with --document-private-items (the reachable surface). model.py diffs them into a
`visibility` column. See build/README.md and reference.md limit 3.
The wiring crate set is indexed because datafusion-tracing cannot be used without a
tracing-subscriber, and its versions are the ones THIS release of datafusion-tracing is
known to compose with -- taken from examples/Cargo.toml at tag 55.0.0, not from crates.io
latest, which has already moved a minor ahead on both otel lines.
DataFusion, Arrow and object_store are deliberately NOT indexed. Their access paths land in
unresolved.tsv. That is a boundary, not a gap.

repository.name: datafusion-tracing
repository.title: datafusion-tracing, instrumented-object-store, and the tracing/OpenTelemetry wiring
repository.description: Pinned API surface, macro grammar, emitted span contract, executed probes and the version-compatibility matrix for DataFusion query instrumentation.

_rustdoc_format_note: docs.rs serves this crate set at FIVE different format versions, because it builds on
its own schedule and its fleet is not uniform. Measured 2026-09-17: the subject crates
and tracing/tracing-core at 61, tracing-subscriber at 59, tracing-futures at 60, and all
four OpenTelemetry crates at 56 -- older than any sibling repository in this family has
had to parse. 56 was not added on the assumption that it is close enough: acquire.py
asserts the field vocabulary model.py depends on is present in every document it accepts,
so a format that merely parses far enough to produce confident nonsense is a stop.

probe_toolchain.note: The probes build on STABLE, because a probe is a claim about what a consumer will observe and a consumer builds on stable. Pinned rather than inherited: this workstation's rustup default is nightly, and the first run of probes.py silently reported what a nightly compiler produced. datafusion-tracing 55.0.0 declares rust-version 1.94.0, so any stable at or above it works; 1.98.1 is the one recorded here.

local_rustdoc.note: A recorded producer identity, not a build configuration. The dated form is required: a bare +nightly floats, and a floating producer cannot be re-pinned.

crates.note: 12 macro_rules! macros, 2 option structs, 1 formatter fn, 2 doc(hidden) fns.
tracing::instrument is a re-export of this crate's proc macro. Without it the access path resolves to nothing, and #[instrument] is the first thing anyone reaches for.
